title: Two Views of the Missions: Sin Embargo, No Obstante and Aunque

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *sin embargo* from A2 Unit 28 and *no obstante* from B1 Unit 1, and *aunque* from A2 Unit 28. They introduce an idea that goes against the first one. The Jesuit missions are a topic where historians disagree, so they are very useful to put two views side by side.

sections.title: Contrast connectors
rows: Las misiones protegieron a los guaraníes; sin embargo, los jesuitas controlaban su vida.
Los jesuitas fueron expulsados en 1767; no obstante, las ruinas siguen en pie.
Aunque la iglesia de Jesús quedó sin terminar, hoy es patrimonio de la humanidad.
La música barroca llegó de Europa; sin embargo, los guaraníes la hicieron suya.

items.spanish: Las misiones protegieron a los guaraníes; sin embargo, los jesuitas controlaban su vida.
items.english: The missions protected the Guaraní; however, the Jesuits controlled their lives.

items.spanish: Los jesuitas fueron expulsados en 1767; no obstante, las ruinas siguen en pie.
items.english: The Jesuits were expelled in 1767; nevertheless, the ruins are still standing.

items.spanish: Aunque la iglesia de Jesús quedó sin terminar, hoy es patrimonio de la humanidad.
items.english: Although the church of Jesús was left unfinished, it is a world heritage site today.

items.spanish: La música barroca llegó de Europa; sin embargo, los guaraníes la hicieron suya.
items.english: Baroque music came from Europe; however, the Guaraní made it their own.

sections.content: Use a contrast connector only when the second idea goes against the first; for a result use *por eso* or *así que*. *Sin embargo* and *no obstante* take a comma after them. When historians disagree, say who holds each view (*según algunos historiadores*).
